## Purpose
A backward-compatibility alias. The old import path resolves to the very same module object as `app.catalog.autotag`, which itself aliases `app.catalog.tagging`, so both old names resolve to the tagging module.

## Responsibilities
It imports `app.catalog.autotag` and replaces its own entry in `sys.modules` with it: `sys.modules[__name__] = _moved`.

## Key elements
None of its own. Every name belongs to `app.catalog.autotag`.

## Control flow
Runs once, at import.

## Data, state and side effects
It mutates `sys.modules`.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- Old imports, and test patches that target the old path.
- New code imports `app.catalog.autotag` directly.

## Error handling and edge cases
None.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **It aliases the module object, not a copy.** A `mock.patch` on the old path patches the real module, and SQLAlchemy models are not registered twice.
- **Keep the file as long as anything imports the old name.**

## How to rebuild this file
A docstring saying where the module moved, then `import sys`, `from app.catalog import autotag as _moved` and `sys.modules[__name__] = _moved`.

## Tests
Covered indirectly by tests that import the old paths.
